title: The five consistency levels and what each one costs

videos.script: Quitanda's orders live in Cosmos DB, and Cosmos DB keeps more than one copy of each of them. {{replicas}} A write lands on some copies first, and the others catch up a moment later. So a read can reach a copy that has not heard of the newest write yet. {{lag}} Cosmos DB lets you choose how much of that a reader may see. There are five levels, from strong to eventual. {{spectrum}} Strong never shows an old value. Eventual promises only that the copies agree in the end. Between them sit bounded staleness, session and consistent prefix. {{middle}} Every step towards strong is paid for. Reads cost twice the request units at the top two levels, writes wait longer across regions, and one arrangement of regions is refused outright. {{cost}} Session is the default, and it works through a token. Every write hands one back, and a read that carries it is never served an older copy. {{token}} You will watch that token on the emulator, and see a read refused for carrying one from the future. {{refused}} The emulator keeps a single copy of everything, so it can never show you a stale read. This lesson says each place where that matters. {{emulator}}
